headline: On November 22, 1987: Max Headroom hijacks Chicago TV signals
captionCards: Unidentified hacker used a Max Headroom mask to hijack two Chicago stations
The incident revealed flaws in broadcast security and influenced digital media art
instagramCaption:
A masked figure interrupts Chicago TV broadcasts.

Two stations were hijacked in the same day by an unknown person wearing a Max Headroom mask. The pirate broadcast aired for minutes during prime time. The hijacker used a signal-stealing device to override live feeds. This remains one of the most famous cases of broadcast intrusion in U.S. history.

It exposed vulnerabilities in analog television systems and inspired future media art and hacker culture.
